Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR batches durable chat input acceptance, transcript promotion, and run adoption through the existing session actor. **Example:** Send ten warmed chat turns in the pinned comparison workload. - **Before:** Median all-thread SQLite work averages 657.1 statements per turn. - **After:** The candidate averages 594.8 statements per turn while retaining durable input before acknowledgment. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A useful measured cutover with meaningful boundary coverage and no new actionable finding; accepted tradeoffs remain explicit. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (linked_artifact): The previously assessed Gateway workloads exercise acceptance and adoption through startup, connected chat turns, and shutdown; later recorded regressions cover committed custody, cancellation, lifecycle replacement, and transaction/commit refusal. Linked proof portals were inaccessible here, which does not invalidate the retained evidence. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Performance · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Chat acceptance and run startup repeatedly read session facts and perform separate durable writes. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction has measured incremental savings and explicitly records retained costs and accepted ordering tradeoffs. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 1 item remains** Keep this PR open: it delivers a measured performance improvement beyond the landed actor core. No new actionable code finding remains after the maintainer explicitly accepted the earlier completion interleaving; GitHub still reports conflicts and failed required CI. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `536d9d4fa54c98b54a95148e61c387062624fd80` ## Before merge - [ ] **Complete next step** - Resolve GitHub's reported conflicts with main and validate the affected session and Gateway contracts after the resolution. ## Findings None.

This performance refactor has pinned comparative measurements and custody regressions; the separate hosted optional-identity failure has no established root cause. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Reusing the admitted actor and existing transaction kernels addresses repeated database work without adding a competing writer or replay protocol. In https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168607#issuecomment-6107664327, steipete expressly accepts that exact successor interleaving for this landing without claiming it fixed. ([`src/config/sessions/session-turn.ts:672`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/536d9d4fa54c98b54a95148e61c387062624fd80/src/config/sessions/session-turn.ts#L672), [536d9d4fa54c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/536d9d4fa54c98b54a95148e61c387062624fd80)) - **Committed custody and final authority:** Committed pending custody publishes before callbacks, and the final actor commit admission carries the exact turn candidate.
